title: User Stories & Acceptance Criteria
description: Write clear, testable user stories and define done. Tests story writing, Given/When/Then criteria, and story mapping.

seo.overviewTitle: Agile User Stories & Acceptance Criteria (Gherkin Syntax)
seo.overviewBody: User stories define product requirements from the end user's perspective. Agile teams assess business analysts on writing stories using standard syntax ('As a... I want... So that...'), adhering to INVEST quality criteria, and defining testable acceptance criteria in Gherkin (Given-When-Then) format.

deliverables.title: 1. Agile User Story Backlog Specification
deliverables.desc: Product backlog document containing well-structured user stories complete with user personas and business value justifications.

deliverables.title: 2. Gherkin Acceptance Criteria Test Suite
deliverables.desc: Acceptance criteria library written in Given-When-Then format covering happy path and edge-case scenarios.

deliverables.title: 3. INVEST Criteria Quality Audit Log
deliverables.desc: Quality assurance checklist verifying user stories meet INVEST standards before sprint planning.

faqs.question: What does the INVEST acronym stand for in user stories?
faqs.answer: Independent, Negotiable, Valuable, Estimable, Small, and Testable.

faqs.question: How do you write acceptance criteria using Gherkin syntax?
faqs.answer: Given [initial context/state], When [action occurs], Then [expected outcome/behavior].

faqs.question: What is the difference between a User Story and a System Requirement?
faqs.answer: A User Story focuses on end-user needs and value ('As a shopper...'). A System Requirement specifies technical mechanics ('The database shall encrypt stored credit card numbers').
